newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-JONES EXTENDS PHOENIX OPEN LEAD TO FIVE AFTER TWO ROUNDS.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-JONES EXTENDS PHOENIX OPEN LEAD TO FIVE AFTER TWO ROUNDS.

text.p: Steve Jones fired a seven-under-par 64 Friday to extend his lead at the Phoenix Open to five strokes and go 16 under par after two rounds, equalling the best start ever on the PGA Tour.
He is the fifth PGA player to shoot 126 in a tournament's first 36 holes.
David Duval and Tommy Tolles shot six-under par scores of 65 to stand five strokes back.
One stroke further back at 10 under par were Sweden's Jesper Parnevik, who shot 66, and Paul Azinger, whose 63 was his lowest score since he was diagnosed with cancer in 1993.
Tiger Woods was tied for 12th place at six under par, 10 strokes behind Jones, after his second successive round of 68.
Jones nearly missed his tee time on Thursday, and slightly overcompensated by arriving four minutes early on Friday.
"My goal was to put a good round together to follow up the 62, and it worked out pretty decently, except for the second hole," said Jones.

Jones had his only bogey of the tournament on the second hole, a three-putt from 25 feet. He scored most effectively on the back nine, where he shot a five-under 31. He made birdies on the 13th, 14th and 17th holes, and sank a 20-foot putt for eagle on the 15th.

On his record start to the week, the reigning U.S. Open champion said: "It's really neat any time you do something like that, it adds a little something to your tournament. But the main thing is to concentrate the next two days and wrap it up.

"I think about Tom Lehman. That guy is relentless when he gets the lead, he just keeps making it bigger, and you have to have that mind-set. So I'm going to try to have the Tom Lehman mind-set this weekend."
The two men just behind Jones, Duval and Tolles, are players that many people deem most likely to break through this year for a first win.

Like Jones, Tolles and Duval did most of their scoring on the back nine. Tolles had six birdies, four of them in succession. On the front he had three birdies and three bogeys. Duval had five birdies on the back, a bogey and two more birdies on the front.
After his 63, Paul Azinger said that his game was the closest to its 1993 level -- when he won the PGA Championship -- that it has been since his illness.

"I've been playing well for a few months now," he said. "I was 46 under par for my last 12 rounds last year. I didn't compete in the off-season, but I worked a lot on my game. Tiger is forcing all of us to practice more.
"All I want to do is get back to playing good again."
